It is thought to be the capital of the Tocobaga, and it was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1964; Pinellas County says the temple mound is the largest remaining mound in the Tampa Bay region.
notes: NHL nomination (NPS, revised June 1981): 'late prehistoric site which was occupied into the early part of the Spanish period (ca. 1500-1650 A.D.)'; mound 'about 150 feet in diameter and about 20 feet in height'; 'generally thought that the Safety Harbor Site may be the Tocobago capitol'. NHL year 1964 from Wikipedia Safety Harbor site. Pinellas County page: 'largest remaining mound in the Tampa Bay region'.

title: Tampa International opens its landside-airside terminal
text: Tampa International Airport's new terminal opened to passengers on April 15, 1971, with a central landside building linked to four airside satellites, a landside-airside design described as the first of its type in the world.
notes: Wikipedia: 'The terminal opened for passenger traffic on April 15, 1971 with four airside satellites (Airsides B, C, D, and E)'; 'Tampa International Airport's Landside/Airside terminal was the first of its type in the world.'

title: The University of South Florida gets its site
text: A 1955 state law created a new state university in Hillsborough County, and on Dec. 18, 1956, the Florida Cabinet chose its site, the former Hillsborough Army Airfield on Fowler Avenue. The University of South Florida held its first classes on Sept. 26, 1960; it describes itself as the first major state university planned, built and opened in the 20th century.
notes: USF history: June 18, 1955, Gov. LeRoy Collins signs House Bill 1007 creating a new state university in Hillsborough County; 'December 18, 1956' Cabinet approves the site, 'the former Hillsborough Army Airfield property on Fowler Avenue'; first classes September 26, 1960; 'the first major state university planned, built and opened in the 20th century'. Raw page: 'USF becomes the first major state university planned, built and opened in the 20th century, as well as Florida's first university located in a major metropolitan area.'

title: Tampa incorporates as a village
text: On Jan. 18, 1849, fourteen men voted unanimously to establish the Village of Tampa with a trustee government, and a week later they elected five trustees. Citizens organized the Town of Tampa on Sept. 10, 1853.
notes: City Clerk: 'January 18, 1849 - 14 men vote unanimously to establish Tampa Village with a trustee form of government.' 'January 25, 1849 - Village of Tampa elects 5 trustees with M.G. Sikes elected president.' 'September 10, 1853 - Citizens vote to organize as the Town of Tampa'. Coordinates: the history-of-tampa point for the incorporation event (27.9475, -82.457), the original downtown.

title: The Vinoy Park Hotel opens on New Year's Eve
text: Aymer Vinoy Laughner's 375-room hotel on the St. Petersburg waterfront, designed by Henry L. Taylor, went up in just under 10 months from Feb. 5, 1925, and opened on New Year's Eve 1925. It became an Army Air Forces and Maritime Service training center in 1942, closed in 1974 and reopened in 1992 after restoration; it operates today as The Vinoy Resort & Golf Club.
notes: The Vinoy history: construction began 'on February 5, 1925' under architect Henry L. Taylor and contractor George A. Miller, 'the 375-room hotel in just under 10 months, in time for a grand opening on New Year's Eve 1925'; 'On July 3, 1942, The Vinoy ceased operation as a hotel and was leased to the U.S. Army Air Force and subsequently the United States Maritime Service as a training center'; 'In 1974, the hotel closed its doors for good'; 'in 1992, The Vinoy reopened as a Stouffer Hotel.' Name of the current operation: stays-stpete-pinellas slice id vinoy-resort-golf-club. Coordinates from that slice.

title: Shipyards and hotels go to war
text: During World War II the Tampa Shipbuilding and Engineering Company and the Hooker's Point Shipyard built ships for the war effort, and Tampa's shipyard workforce reached 16,000. Across the bay St. Petersburg became a major technical training center for the Army Air Corps: more than 100,000 trainees filled the city's hotels, the Vinoy became a training center in July 1942, and the Army turned the Don CeSar into a hospital.
notes: Museum of Florida History: 'Florida shipyards included the Tampa Shipbuilding and Engineering Company (later known as TASCO), the Hooker's Point Shipyard in Tampa'. NRHP North Franklin: 'The personnel at Tampa shipyards reached 16,000'. City of St. Petersburg: 'St. Pete became a major technical services training center for the Army Air Corps. More than 100,000 trainees filled every hotel in the city'. Vinoy: leased July 3, 1942. Don CeSar: Army purchase 1942, hospital. Coordinates: Hooker's Point yard (Photon railway yard name 'Hookers Point Yard'); area: Hooker's Point is the port peninsula by the Channel District.

title: A Smithsonian dig at Weedon Island names a culture
text: Smithsonian Institution archaeologist J. Walter Fewkes excavated a mound on Weedon Island in Old Tampa Bay in 1923 and 1924, and the decorated ceremonial pottery first described there gave its name to the Weeden Island culture of the Southeast. The island, later home to homesteaders, speakeasies, a Hollywood movie studio and a 1930s airport, is now Pinellas County's Weedon Island Preserve.
notes: Wikipedia Weeden Island culture: 'The site on Weedon Island where Weeden Island sacred ceramics were first described was excavated by Smithsonian Institution archaeologist J. Walter Fewkes in 1923 and 1924'; name 'derived from the Weedon Island site (despite the dissimilar spellings) in Old Tampa Bay in Pinellas County'. Preserve history page: 'homesteaders, speakeasies, a Hollywood movie studio and a 1930s airport'. Coordinates: Photon nature_reserve match.

title: Newt Perry opens Weeki Wachee's mermaid show
text: In 1947 stunt swimmer and promoter Newt Perry created the Weeki Wachee attraction, building a theater into the limestone of the spring with windows below the water so visitors could watch 'mermaids' perform. It is now Weeki Wachee Springs State Park.
notes: Wikipedia: 'The attraction was created in 1947 by stunt swimmer and attraction promoter Newt Perry'; 'First an 18-seat theater... were embedded in the lime rock of the spring with viewing windows below the surface of the water'; 'Officially: Weeki Wachee Springs State Park'. floridastateparks.org returns 403.

title: Hugh Macfarlane founds West Tampa
text: In 1892 Scottish businessman Hugh Macfarlane founded West Tampa across the Hillsborough River as a second cigar town; by 1900 it was one of the most populous places in Florida, mostly Cuban cigar workers. Together Ybor City and West Tampa made Tampa, in the National Park Service's words, the hand-rolled cigar capital of the world by 1900. Tampa annexed West Tampa in 1925.
notes: History of Tampa (Wikipedia): 'In 1892, Scottish businessman Hugh MacFarlane founded West Tampa... By 1900, the town already had one of the largest populations in Florida, mostly Cubans involved in the cigar industry'; 'Also in 1925... Tampa annexed the neighboring town of West Tampa.' NHL: 'By 1900 Tampa had become the hand-rolled cigar capital of the world... In addition to Ybor City, another cigar-making community, West Tampa, grew up'.

title: John C. Williams buys the land that becomes St. Petersburg
text: In 1875 John Constantine Williams of Detroit bought 2,500 acres of waterfront land on the lower Pinellas peninsula. Thirteen years later he traded part of it to Peter Demens so that Demens's Orange Belt Railroad would reach his settlement.
notes: City of St. Petersburg: 'In 1875 John Constantine Williams of Detroit, Michigan moved to Tampa and bought 2,500 acres of warm waterfront land that would eventually become St. Petersburg. Thirteen years later, he transferred part of that land to Peter Demens... In exchange, Demens extended the Orange Belt Railroad to Williams's settlement.'

title: Students sit in at the Woolworth lunch counter
text: On Feb. 29, 1960, about 40 students from Middleton and Blake high schools, led by Clarence Fort and the Rev. A. Leon Lowry, staged a peaceful sit-in at the F. W. Woolworth lunch counter at 901 N. Franklin St. By September 1960 Tampa's lunch counters were integrated without the violence seen in many other places.
notes: City of Tampa Soulwalk marker (verbatim facts). Coordinates: 901 N Franklin St (census).

title: Vicente Martínez Ybor agrees to move his cigar business to Tampa
text: On Oct. 5, 1885, cigar maker Vicente Martínez Ybor contracted with the Tampa Board of Trade to move his hand-rolled cigar business, Ybor & Co., from Key West to Tampa. He bought 40 acres northeast of the town, and work began that October clearing the land for a factory and 50 houses.
notes: LoC: 'contracted with the Tampa Board of Trade on October 5, 1885, to relocate his hand rolled cigar manufacturing business Ybor & Co.'; 'Ybor purchased 40 acres of land northeast of Tampa'. NHL nomination: 'began developing the land he had purchased near Tampa in October 1885... Workmen felled trees, cleared underbrush... Ybor contracted for a wooden factory and 50 houses'. Coordinates: the Ybor factory, 1916 N 14th St (census).

title: Tampa annexes Ybor City
text: Ybor City's rapid growth led Tampa to annex it in June 1887, although the cigar town kept its own identity; by 1890 it had about 6,000 residents, more than the rest of Tampa. The following month, on July 15, 1887, Tampa organized under a new city charter that also absorbed the Town of North Tampa.
notes: NHL: 'in June 1887, it became legally part of that city, although it maintained its separate identity... by 1890 it had a population of around 6,000, which outnumbered the native residents of Tampa.' City Clerk: July 15, 1887 charter abolishing the Town of Tampa and Town of North Tampa governments. Coordinates: Ybor City Museum State Park (census, 1818 E 9th Ave).

title: Ybor City's first cigar factories open
text: Ignacio Haya's factory went into production first, in March 1886, and Ybor's own factory followed; by the end of 1886 several hundred worker houses stood between today's 6th and 9th avenues and 12th and 14th streets, and more than 3,000 workers had come from Cuba. The 1886 V. M. Ybor factory on 14th Street, the first brick cigar factory built in Tampa, still stands.
notes: NHL nomination: 'enabled Haya to get into production first, in March 1886'; 'By the end of the year, over 3,000, some 15% of whom were Black, had arrived'; 'By the end of 1886... In the area between present 6th and 9th Avenues and from 12th to 14th Streets, the Ybor and Haya cigar factories were in full operation, several hundred worker houses completed and occupied'. LoC: 'The original building was the first brick cigar factory constructed in Tampa in 1886.'

title: Fire destroys 350 buildings in Ybor City
text: A fire in 1908 destroyed 350 buildings in Ybor City between 16th and 20th streets and 12th and Michigan (now Columbus Drive) avenues. Rebuilding replaced many frame buildings with brick, and into the 1930s owners added the wrought-iron balconies, stucco and Spanish tile that give 7th Avenue its look.
notes: NHL: 'many frame commercial and commercial-residential buildings were replaced with brick ones, particularly after a disastrous fire in 1908, in which 350 buildings were destroyed in the area between 16th and 20th Streets and 12th and Michigan Avenues (Columbus Drive). Also, during this period, and into the 1930s, many property owners added wrought-iron balconies, stucco, and Spanish tile'.

title: Ybor City's historic district is listed on the National Register
text: The Ybor City Historic District, mainly the 7th Avenue commercial corridor and its cigar factories, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974; a larger district was later designated a National Historic Landmark. The state bought the 1923 Ferlita Bakery in 1976 and opened it as the Ybor City State Museum in 1980.
notes: NHL nomination: 'National Register Historic District, listed in 1974, which includes mainly the 7th Avenue commercial corridor and adjoining cigar factories'; the NHL boundary adds residential areas. 'The State acquired the Ferlita Bakery in 1976, restored it, and opened it to the public as the Ybor City State Museum in 1980.' 'The bakery was built in 1923'. NPS place page: 'Designation: National Historic Landmark' (date not given).

title: Urban renewal and I-4 cut through Ybor City
text: In 1965 Ybor City became the target of a major urban renewal project: over the next few years 70 acres, including 660 frame houses, two ethnic club buildings, a fire station and a cigarmakers' school, were leveled, and the promised redevelopment largely never came. Construction of Interstate 4 also split the community, but the losses spurred Tampa's Latin community to preserve its culture and landmark buildings.
notes: NHL: 'In 1965 Ybor City became the target of a major urban renewal project. During the next few years, 70 acres, including 660 frame houses, two ethnic club buildings, a fire station, and a cigarmakers' school were leveled. Although plans for redevelopment were announced, they largely came to naught because expected Federal urban renewal money did not materialize. The construction of Interstate 4 also split the community.' 'the renewal project sparked a revival of interest in the area among the Latin community to preserve its culture and most significant buildings.'
